competences: The learner identifies facts about roles of district officials.
The learner states responsibilities and qualities of leaders in the district.
languageCompetence: Pronounce, read and spell district, leader, officer, responsibility, appointment and service.
objectives: By the end of the lesson learners should identify the key points about roles of district officials.
By the end of the lesson learners should answer five original district-leadership questions.
priorKnowledge: Learners have already studied district leaders, local councils and the services provided by appointed officials.
materials: Chart of district leaders and their duties
references: P4 Social Studies Notes for Terms 1–3

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher introduces roles of district officials and asks "5. State any one role performed by the chairperson on the LC I executive committee." to recall prior knowledge. They collect learners' responses and relate them to district leadership.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall earlier work on political and civic leaders, answer the starter question and name a district official.

steps.stage: Development: Duties of the district chairperson
steps.content: The district chairperson coordinates local-government activities. The district chairperson appoints other officials. The district chairperson supervises local officers. The chairperson monitors district administration. District councils plan community development projects.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the source-grounded points on duties of the district chairperson, starting with "The district chairperson coordinates local-government activities. The district chairperson appoints other officials." They check knowledge using the original question "6. How is the LCI vice chairperson useful to children in your community?" and explain corrections.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners identify the relevant officials or leadership qualities, answer questions, and copy correct points into their books.

steps.stage: Development: Duties of the Resident District Commissioner
steps.content: The RDC represents the president in the district. The RDC chairs district security meetings. The RDC advises district chairpersons on national matters. The RDC coordinates central-government activities. The RDC helps implement central-government policies.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the source-grounded points on duties of the resident district commissioner, starting with "The RDC represents the president in the district. The RDC chairs district security meetings." They check knowledge using the original question "8. State any three problems district leaders face when carrying out their duties." and explain corrections.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners identify the relevant officials or leadership qualities, answer questions, and copy correct points into their books.

steps.stage: Development: Duties of health, education and agricultural officials
steps.content: The DDHS supervises district health centres. The DDHS guides workers during disease outbreaks. The DEO oversees district education programmes. The DEO improves standards in district schools. The agricultural officer teaches farmers good farming methods. The veterinary officer advises livestock farmers.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the source-grounded points on duties of health, education and agricultural officials, starting with "The DDHS supervises district health centres. The DDHS guides workers during disease outbreaks." They check knowledge using the original question "9. Mention any three roles played by the LC I council in the village." and explain corrections.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners identify the relevant officials or leadership qualities, answer questions, and copy correct points into their books.

steps.stage: Development: Duties of other district officers
steps.content: The district police commander maintains law and order. The district water officer distributes clean water. The forestry officer encourages planting of trees. The fisheries officer fights illegal fishing. The district engineer helps build roads and bridges. The district sports officer manages sports activities.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the source-grounded points on duties of other district officers, starting with "The district police commander maintains law and order. The district water officer distributes clean water." They check knowledge using the original question "14. How is the Secretary for defense useful on the Local council I committee?" and explain corrections.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners identify the relevant officials or leadership qualities, answer questions, and copy correct points into their books.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the supplied questions, beginning with "5. State any one role performed by the chairperson on the LC I executive committee." and "6. How is the LCI vice chairperson useful to children in your community?". They monitor learners' written answers, then mark and explain them using the reference notes.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the questions individually, consult the notes and correct their written responses after marking.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher checks understanding with "8. State any three problems district leaders face when carrying out their duties." and "9. Mention any three roles played by the LC I council in the village.". They review the relevant factual points and assign the final question for revision.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners give oral answers, state an important point and record the sourced homework question.

assessment: Check the original questions "5. State any one role performed by the chairperson on the LC I executive committee.", "6. How is the LCI vice chairperson useful to children in your community?", and "8. State any three problems district leaders face when carrying out their duties."; mark against the sourced facts.
